transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's planning roundtable. As you know, the middle school has proposed a six-week peer-tutoring program for students in grades 6 through 8, and before I sign off on the approval, I want to make sure we've thoroughly reviewed the plan from all angles. The draft currently calls for two adult supervisors, Google Classroom for session communication, student-selected tutor pairings, and paper consent forms collected before the program begins. I'd like to go around the table and hear from each of you about any concerns or considerations related to your area of expertise. Let's start with you -- what should I know before I set the operating requirements for this program?

transcript.text: I need to flag an important staffing issue. Yesterday I received the finalized roster from the activities office, and it contains 18 student tutors. The school's supervision rule permits one adult to supervise no more than six tutors in an active tutoring session. That means with 18 tutors, we'd need at least three adult supervisors, not two. The draft plan still lists the preliminary staffing estimate of two supervisors, so we'll need to update that before approval.

Because of this, tutor pairings cannot be left to student selection -- I will need to assign and monitor all pairings myself to ensure we don't inadvertently place students together in violation of those no-contact restrictions.
